# std.seq

Sequences: reductions, scans, runs, searching, permutations, monotone stacks, and compression.   - Reductions & extrema: `prod`, `is_sorted`, `min`/`max` (with `by:`), `argmax`/`argmin` (with `by:`). - Binary & unimodal search: moved to `std.search` (`ternary_max`/`ternary_min`, `Range<F64>.bsearch`/`peak`/`valley`, `parallel_bsearch`). - Sorted lookup: `first_ge`/`first_gt`/`last_le`/`last_lt` (with optional `by:`), returning `?D` on `[D]T`, `?Int` on `List<T>`, and `?(K, V)` on `Map<K, V>`. - Runs, chunking & windows: `runs` (with `by:` or `link:`), `buckets`, `windows`, `chunks`, `adjacent`, `pairs`, `with_prev`, `cyclic_pairs`, `zip`. - Scans & folds: `scan` (`.rev.scan` for suffixes); the fold of everything but `i` is `op(pre[i.l], suf[i.r])` over `a.scan(op)` and `a.rev.scan(op)`. - Reordering & selection: `reverse`, `rotate_left`/`rotate_right`, `dedup`/`deduped`, `partition`, `select`, `merge_sorted`. - Permutations: `next_permutation`, `prev_permutation`, `inverse`, `compose`, `perm_cycles`, `perm_pow`, `inversions`. - Nearest smaller: `prev_smaller`/`next_smaller` (larger with `by: desc`), `prev_same`/`next_same`, `MonoStack`; sliding windows fold with `a.window_fold(k, op)` or `Window(op)` (`std.window`). - Coordinate compression: `let (domain C, xs) = compress(all)` -> `Compressed<C, T>` (`index_of`, `try_index_of`, `contains`, `first_ge`, `first_gt`, `last_le`, `last_lt`).

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Anchor`, `Bidir`, `Compressed`, `Indexed`, `Keyed`, `Perm`, `Positional`, `Rev`, `RingSlice`, `Seq`, `Sized`, `Slice`, `Stepped`, `Ties`, `Track`, `adjacent`, `all`, `any`, `buckets`, `chain`, `chunks`, `compress`, `count`, `cyclic_pairs`, `dedup`, `deduped`, `distinct`, `drop_while`, `each`, `equal_range`, `find`, `first_gt`, `flat_map`, `flatten`, `get_or_insert`, `group`, `inverse`, `inversions`, `is_sorted`, `is_subsequence`, `iterate`, `last_lt`, `len`, `lis`, `next_permutation`, `pairs`, `partition`, `prev_permutation`, `prod`, `product`, `reduce`, `reverse`, `reversed`, `rotate_left`, `rotate_right`, `rotated_left`, `rotated_right`, `runs`, `select`, `span`, `step`, `sum`, `take_while`, `windows`, `zip`.

## Types & Constants

- `type Perm<V> = [V]V` — Every value of `V` once, in some order.

## `enum Ties`

Which of several equal best elements an extreme returns: `Ties.First` or `Ties.Last` in sequence order.

## `struct Compressed<D, T>(vals: [D]T)`

The distinct values of a coordinate compression, in increasing order, indexed by their own domain `D`.

- `fn get(self, i: D) -> T` — \(O(1)\)
- `fn slice(self, r: Range<D>) -> List<T>` — \(O(r.\mathit{len})\); The compressed values over a range `r` of `xs.D`, as a list.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); How many distinct values there are.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether no value was compressed.
- `@get fn items(self) -> yields (D, T)` — \(O(\mathit{len})\)
- `fn index_of(self, val: T) -> D` — \(O(\log n)\); The index of `val`, which must be one of the compressed values.; traps: when `val` was not compressed
- `fn try_index_of(self, val: T) -> ?D` — \(O(\log n)\); The index of `val` if it was compressed, or `None`.
- `fn contains(self, val: T) -> Bool` — \(O(\log n)\); Whether `val` is one of the compressed values.
- `fn first_ge(self, val: T) -> ?D` — \(O(\log n)\); The first index whose value is `>= val`, or `None`.
- `fn first_gt(self, val: T) -> ?D` — \(O(\log n)\); The first index whose value is `> val`, or `None`.
- `fn last_le(self, val: T) -> ?D` — \(O(\log n)\); The last index whose value is `<= val`, or `None`.
- `fn last_lt(self, val: T) -> ?D` — \(O(\log n)\); The last index whose value is `< val`, or `None`.

## `trait Seq<T>`

A sequence: `for x in s` walks it in order, and each `for` runs it from the start (R07.3.1).

## `trait Keyed<D, T>: Seq<T>`

A `Seq` whose elements carry keys: `s.items` walks `(key, x)`, and keys survive `filter` (R07.3.2).

## `trait Sized`

A sequence with an \(O(1)\) length (R07.3.3).

## `trait Bidir<T>: Seq<T>`

A `Seq` that can also walk from its end, which is what `.rev` needs.

## `trait Positional<T>: Seq<T> + Sized`

A sized sequence read in \(O(1)\) by walk position: `s.nth(k)` is the element `k` steps into the walk.

## `trait IndexGet<K, T>`

`s[k]` read: the element at key `k`.

## `trait IndexMut<K, T>: IndexGet<K, T>`

`s[k]` as a place: a write through it lands in `s`, in place (R12.4.6).

## `trait IndexedMut<K, T>: Indexed<K, T> + IndexMut<K, T>`

An `Indexed` sequence whose cells are places: what `sort`, `reverse` and `swap` write (R12.4.6).

## `trait IndexSet<K, T>`

`s[k] = v` as a write of `v` at `k`, not through a place: a `Map` inserts or replaces, and its values need no default (spec 12, W8).

## `trait Indexed<D, T>: IndexGet<D, T> + Keyed<D, T> + Positional<T> + Bidir<T>`

A keyed, sized, two-way sequence read in \(O(1)\) at any key; `take`/`drop` give a slice.

## `trait Sep<T>`

What `split(sep:)` cuts at: an element equal to a value, or one where a predicate holds (decision 456).

## `enum Anchor`

Which end of a piece a two-pointer result is keyed by.

## `trait Track<T>`

State a window can add to at the back and remove from at the front.

## `struct Ring<D, T>(pub src: [D]T)`

`a.ring`; see `ring`.

- `fn step(self, i: D, d: Int) -> D` — \(O(1)\); The position `d` steps after `i` (before it when `d < 0`), wrapping: a forced-online decode `(v + last - 1) % n + 1` is `V.ring.step(v, last)`.
- `fn next(self, i: D) -> D` — \(O(1)\); The position after `i`, wrapping.
- `fn prev(self, i: D) -> D` — \(O(1)\); The position before `i`, wrapping.
- `fn from(self, i: D) -> yields D` — \(O(1)\) per step; All n positions, starting at `i` and wrapping.
- `fn span(self, start: D, len: Int) -> RingRange<D>` — \(O(1)\); The `len` positions from `start` on, wrapping (`len <= n`).; traps: when `len` is not in `0..=n`
- `fn windows(self, k: Int) -> RingWindows<D, T>` — \(O(1)\) to build, \(O(1)\) per window walked; The n windows of `k` elements, one starting at each position, wrapping.; traps: when `k` is not in `1..=n`
- `fn maximal<St: Track<T>>(self, state: St, ok: St -> Bool) -> [D]RingSlice<D, T>` — \(O(n)\) pushes and pops on `state`; Two pointers round the cycle: for each position as the last element, the longest wrapping piece (at most n elements) ending there that is `ok`, fed through `state: Track`.
- `fn minimal<St: Track<T>>(self, state: St, ok: St -> Bool) -> [D]?RingSlice<D, T>` — \(O(n)\) pushes and pops on `state`; For each position as the last element, the shortest wrapping piece ending there that is `ok`, or None.

## `struct RingWindows<D, T>(pub src: Ring<D, T>, k: Int)`

A contiguous piece of a ring, possibly wrapping past the end, at most n elements.

Fields: `k: Int,`.

## Functions

- `fn prod<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S) -> T where T: One` — \(O(n)\); Product of all elements of `self` (`T.one` when empty).; traps: never (overflow wraps in release, traps in debug)
- `fn sum<S: Seq<T>, T, U: Zero + Add>(self: S, of: T -> U = x => x) -> U` — \(O(n)\); Sum of all elements (`T.zero` when empty), on any `Seq` of a type with `+`; `of:` maps each element first (`xs.sum(of: x => x * x)`).; traps: never (overflow wraps in release, traps in debug)
- `fn mean<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, of: T -> F64 = x => F64(x)) -> ?F64` — \(O(n)\); The average of `of` over the elements as `F64`; `None` when empty.
- `fn min<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x, ties: Ties = Ties.First) -> ?T` — \(O(n)\); The least element by `by`, the first on ties (`ties: Ties.Last` for the last); `None` when empty.
- `fn max<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x, ties: Ties = Ties.First) -> ?T` — \(O(n)\); The greatest element by `by`, the first on ties (`ties: Ties.Last` for the last); `None` when empty.
- `fn minmax<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x) -> ?(T, T)` — \(O(n)\); The least and greatest elements by `by` in one pass, the first of each on ties; `None` when empty.
- `fn count<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, p: T -> Bool = _ => true) -> Int` — \(O(n)\); How many elements satisfy `p` (every element without `p`).
- `fn any<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, p: T -> Bool) -> Bool` — \(O(n)\), stopping at the first match; Whether some element satisfies `p`; stops at the first.
- `fn all<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, p: T -> Bool) -> Bool` — \(O(n)\), stopping at the first failure; Whether every element satisfies `p`; stops at the first that doesn't.
- `fn is_sorted<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x) -> Bool` — \(O(n)\); Whether `self` is non-decreasing (optionally under key `by:`).
- `fn filter<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, p: T -> Bool) -> Filtered<S, T>` — \(O(1)\) to make; \(O(n)\) calls of `p` per walk; A view of the elements satisfying `p`, in order.; traps: never (beyond what `p` traps on)
- `fn map<S: Seq<T>, T, U>(self: S, f: T -> U) -> Mapped<S, T, U>` — \(O(1)\) to make; one call of `f` per element read; \(O(1)\) to make.; traps: never (beyond what `f` traps on)
- `@get fn rev<S: Bidir>(self: S) -> Rev<S>` — \(O(1)\)
- `@get fn items<S: Keyed<K, T>, K, T>(self: S) -> Items<S>` — \(O(1)\)
- `@get fn first<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\)
- `@get fn last<S: Bidir<T>, T>(self: S) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\)
- `fn rfind<S: Bidir<T>, T>(self: S, p: T -> Bool) -> ?T` — \(O(n)\) calls of `p` at most; The last element satisfying `p`, `None` if None does; walks backwards and stops there.; traps: never (beyond what `p` traps on)
- `fn sort<S: IndexedMut<D, T>, D: Domain, T, K: Ord>(mut self: S; by: T -> K = x => x, cmp: ?((T, T) -> Bool) = None)` — \(O(n \log n)\) comparisons, \(O(n)\) extra space; Sort `self` in place by `by`; descending is a key, `by: x => desc(x)`.; traps: in `cpl run` and `--checked`, when `cmp` is not a strict weak order (`cmp(x, x)`, or both `cmp(a, b)` and `cmp(b, a)`); otherwise never (beyond what `by` or `cmp` traps on)
- `fn sorted<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: S; by: T -> K = x => x, cmp: ?((T, T) -> Bool) = None) -> List<T>` — \(O(n \log n)\) comparisons, \(O(n)\) space; The elements of `self` sorted by `by` or `cmp`: the value form of `sort`.; traps: as `sort`
- `fn reversed<S: Bidir<T>, T>(self: S) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\)
- `fn reverse<S: IndexedMut>(mut self: S, range: ?Range<Int> = None)` — \(O(n)\), \(O(1)\) extra space; \(O(n)\).; traps: when `range` falls outside the keys
- `fn dedup<T: Eq>(mut self: List<T>)` — \(O(n)\), \(O(1)\) extra space; \(O(n)\).
- `fn deduped<S: Seq<T>, T: Eq>(self: S) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\); `self` without each value equal to the one before it: the value form of `dedup`, as `sorted` is of `sort`.
- `fn record_highs<D, T, K: Ord>(self: [D]T, by: T -> K = x => x) -> yields D` — \(O(1)\) per step; \(O(n)\).
- `fn distinct<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Hash + Eq>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\) expected, \(O(n)\) extra space; Distinct values of `self` in first-seen order (optionally keyed by `by:`).
- `fn partition<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, keep: T -> Bool) -> (List<T>, List<T>)` — \(O(n)\); The values of `self` that `keep` holds for, then the ones it does not, each in the order they came.
- `fn select<S: IndexedMut<D, T>, D: Domain, T, K: Ord>(mut self: S, k: Int, by: T -> K = x => x, cmp: ?((T, T) -> Bool) = None)` — \(O(n)\) expected, \(O(n \log n)\) worst case, \(O(1)\) extra space; traps: when `k` is not in `0..self.len`
- `fn merge_sorted<A: Positional<T>, B: Positional<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: A, b: B, by: T -> K = x => x) -> yields T` — \(O(1)\) per step and \(O(1)\) memory, so a whole walk is \(O(\lvert a \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\); `.collect()` keeps it as a `List`; \(O(1)\) per step, \(O(1)\) memory.; traps: never; unsorted inputs give an unspecified interleaving
- `fn windows<S: Indexed>(self: S, k: 1..) -> yields Slice<S>` — \(O(1)\) per window; traps: when `k < 1`
- `fn chunks<S: Indexed>(self: S, k: 1..) -> yields Slice<S>` — \(O(1)\) per chunk; traps: when `k < 1`
- `@get fn adjacent<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S) -> yields (T, T)` — \(O(1)\) per step; Adjacent pairs `(prev, x)` of `self`, left to right: `[10, 20, 30].adjacent` gives `(10, 20)` then `(20, 30)`.
- `fn pairs<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S) -> yields (T, T)` — \(O(n^2)\) to walk, \(O(1)\) per pair; Every pair `(x, y)` with `x` before `y`: `[10, 20, 30].pairs()` gives `(10, 20)`, `(10, 30)`, `(20, 30)`.
- `@get fn with_prev<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S) -> yields (?T, T)` — \(O(1)\) per step; Every element paired with the one before it, starting with `(None, first)`: `[10, 20, 30].with_prev` gives `(None, 10)`, `(10, 20)`, `(20, 30)`.
- `fn cyclic_pairs<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S) -> yields (T, T)` — \(O(1)\) per step; Every element with the one after it, the last with the first: the sides of a polygon, the links of a ring.
- `fn zip<A: Seq<T>, B: Positional<U>, T, U>(a: A, b: B) -> Zipped<A, B, T, U>` — \(O(\min(\lvert a \rvert, \lvert b \rvert))\); The pairs `(x, b.nth(i))` for the `i`th `x` that `a` walks, as many as the shorter sequence has.
- `fn unzip<S: Seq<(A, B)>, A, B>(self: S) -> (List<A>, List<B>)` — \(O(n)\), two new lists; The first and second halves of each pair, as two lists: the inverse of `zip`.
- `fn get_or_insert<K: Ord, V>(mut self: Map<K, V>, k: K, v: V) -> V` — \(O(\log n)\); The value `m` holds for `k`, after storing `v` there if it held none: `ids.get_or_insert(name, ids.len)` gives each new name the next id.
- `fn update<K: Ord, V>(mut self: Map<K, V>, k: K, init: V, f: fn(V) -> V)` — \(O(\log n)\), plus one call of `f`; Replace the value under `k` by `f` of it, starting from `init` when `m` holds none: `cnt.update(x, 0, c => c + 1)`.
- `fn union<T: Ord>(mut self: Set<T>, o: Set<T>)` — \(O(m \log(n + m))\) for `m` elements in `o`; Add every element of `o` to `self` in place: `self \| o`, named as on `Bitset`.
- `fn intersect<T: Ord>(mut self: Set<T>, o: Set<T>)` — \(O(n \log m)\) for `m` elements in `o`; Keep only the elements of `self` that are also in `o`, in place: `self & o`, named as on `Bitset`.
- `fn subtract<T: Ord>(mut self: Set<T>, o: Set<T>)` — \(O(m \log n)\) for `m` elements in `o`; Take every element of `o` out of `self` in place: `self - o`, named as on `Bitset`.
- `fn rotate_left<S: IndexedMut>(mut self: S, k: Int, range: ?Range<Int> = None)` — \(O(n)\), \(O(1)\) extra space; Rotate `self` left by `k` in place (or only the subrange `range` when given): what was at offset `k % len` comes first.; traps: when `range` falls outside the keys
- `fn rotate_right<S: IndexedMut>(mut self: S, k: Int, range: ?Range<Int> = None)` — \(O(n)\), \(O(1)\) extra space; Rotate `self` right by `k` in place (or only the subrange `range` when given).; traps: when `range` falls outside the keys
- `fn rotated_left<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, k: Int) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\); A new list rotated left by `k`: what was at offset `k % len` comes first.
- `fn rotated_right<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, k: Int) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\); A new list rotated right by `k`.
- `fn next_permutation<S: IndexedMut<D, T>, D: Domain, T: Ord>(mut self: S) -> Bool` — \(O(n)\) worst case, amortized \(O(1)\) over all arrangements; Step `self` to the next arrangement in sorted order, in place.
- `fn prev_permutation<S: IndexedMut<D, T>, D: Domain, T: Ord>(mut self: S) -> Bool` — \(O(n)\) worst case, amortized \(O(1)\) over all arrangements; Step `self` to the previous arrangement in sorted order, in place.
- `fn runs<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T, K: Eq>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x, link: ?((T, T) -> Bool) = None) -> yields Slice<S>` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(n)\) to walk; The stretches of equal neighbours (or equal `by:` keys), in order, each a slice of `self`.
- `fn buckets<D, K: Domain>(self: [D]K) -> [K]List<D>` — \(O(\lvert D \rvert + \lvert K \rvert)\) time and memory; Bucket the keys of `self` by value: `b[k]` lists every `i` with `self[i] == k`, in key order.
- `fn compress<S: Seq, T: Ord>(self: S) -> (domain C, Compressed<C, T>)` — \(O(n \log n)\); Coordinate compression: `let (domain C, xs) = compress(all)` sorts the values, drops the duplicates and binds a fresh domain `C` for them.
- `fn pieces<D: Ord, S: Seq>(self: Range<D>, cuts: S) -> (domain P, [P]Range<D>)` — \(O(k \log k)\) for k cuts; Split a range at cuts: `let (domain P, piece) = D.pieces(cuts: cs)` binds a fresh domain of the non-empty pieces between consecutive cuts, with `piece[p]` the `Range<D>` that piece covers.; traps: when a cut lies outside the range
- `fn covering<P, D>(self: [P]Range<D>, r: Range<D>) -> Range<P>` — \(O(\log k)\); The range of pieces exactly covering `r`, whose ends must be among the cuts the pieces were made from (traps otherwise).; traps: when an end of `r` is not one of the cuts
- `fn first_some<S: Seq<T>, T, U>(self: S, f: T -> ?U) -> ?U` — \(O(n)\), \(O(1)\) per element walked, stopping at the first `Some`; The first `f(x)` that is not `None`, stopping there; `None` if every one is.
- `fn find<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, p: T -> Bool) -> ?T` — \(O(k)\) calls of `p` for a first match at position \(k\); The first element satisfying `p`, `None` if None does; stops there.
- `fn with_domain<T>(self: List<T>) -> (domain I, [I]T)` — \(O(1)\); moves the list; Gives the items of a list a fresh domain, so arrays over them are index-safe: `let (domain Arc, arcs) = [...].with_domain()`.
- `fn cycle<D>(self: [D]D, from: D) -> yields D` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per step; The cycle of a permutation through `from`: `from`, `perm[from]`, ...; traps: never; a non-permutation that never returns to `from` walks forever
- `fn first_gt<D, T, K: Ord>(self: [D]T, target: K, by: T -> K = x => x) -> ?D` — \(O(\log n)\); First index in sorted `self` with `by(self[i]) > target`, or `None`.; traps: a checked build may trap R0401 on unsorted input, whose search is then wrong-way;
- `fn last_lt<D, T, K: Ord>(self: [D]T, target: K, by: T -> K = x => x) -> ?D` — \(O(\log n)\); Last index in sorted `self` with `by(self[i]) < target`, or `None`.; traps: a checked build may trap R0401 on unsorted input, whose search is then wrong-way;
- `fn inverse<I, V>(self: [I]V) -> [V]I` — \(O(\lvert I \rvert)\); Inverse of bijection `self: [I]V`: `inv[self[i]] == i` for all `i in I`.; traps: when `self` is not a bijection
- `fn compose<A, B, C>(f: [A]B, g: [B]C) -> [A]C` — \(O(\lvert A \rvert)\); Function composition: `compose(f, g)[a] == g[f[a]]`.
- `fn perm_cycles<V>(self: [V]V) -> List<List<V>>` — \(O(\lvert V \rvert)\); Disjoint cycle decomposition of permutation `p`, each cycle starting at its smallest element.; traps: when `p` is not a permutation
- `fn perm_pow<V>(p: [V]V, k: 0..) -> [V]V` — \(O(\lvert V \rvert)\); `k`-th iterate of permutation `p` (`k >= 0`), computed via cycle decomposition.; traps: when `k < 0` or `p` is not a permutation
- `fn inversions<S: Seq<T>, T: Ord>(self: S) -> Int` — \(O(n \log n)\); Number of inversions: pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` and `a[i] > a[j]`.
- `fn swap_at<D, T>(mut self: [D]T, i: D, j: D)` — \(O(1)\); Swap two positions of a domain array in place; safely a no-op when `i == j`.
- `fn swap_idx<S: IndexedMut<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(mut self: S, i: Int, j: Int)` — \(O(1)\); Swap positions `i` and `j` of any `IndexedMut`, counted from 0, in place; a no-op when `i == j`.; traps: when `i` or `j` is not in `0..self.len`
- `fn resized<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(self: S, n: Len, fill: T) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\); `self` cut or padded with `fill` to length `n`: `a.resized(size, Z(0))` instead of `[if i < a.len: a[i] else: Z(0) for i in 0..size]`.; traps: when `n < 0` or `n >= 2^31`
- `fn pop_if<T>(mut self: List<T>, ok: T -> Bool) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\)
- `fn pop_while<T>(mut self: List<T>, ok: T -> Bool) -> List<T>` — \(O(\mathit{popped})\)
- `fn clone<T>(self: T) -> T` — \(O(n)\) for a value of size \(n\), allocates for heap values; \(O(n)\), allocates.
- `fn take_all<T>(mut self: List<T>) -> List<T>` — \(O(1)\); Move all elements out of `self` in \(O(1)\), leaving it empty.
- `fn len<S: Sized>(s: S) -> Int` — what `s.len` costs, \(O(1)\) for every core sequence; The element count of any `Sized` value, as a call: `len(xs)` is `xs.len`.
- `fn drop<S: Indexed>(self: S, k: Len = 1) -> Slice<S>` — \(O(1)\); traps: when `k < 0` or `k >= 2^31`
- `fn drop_last<S: Indexed>(self: S, k: Len = 1) -> Slice<S>` — \(O(1)\); traps: when `k < 0` or `k >= 2^31`
- `fn take<S: Indexed>(self: S, k: Len) -> Slice<S>` — \(O(1)\); traps: when `k < 0` or `k >= 2^31`
- `fn take_last<S: Indexed>(self: S, k: Len) -> Slice<S>` — \(O(1)\); traps: when `k < 0` or `k >= 2^31`
- `fn nth<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(self: S, k: Int) -> T` — \(O(1)\); traps: when `k` is not in `0..self.len`
- `fn to_list<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T>(self: Slice<S>) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\)
- `@get fn rebase<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T>(self: S) -> Rebased<S>` — \(O(1)\)
- `fn step<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T>(self: S, k: 1..) -> Stepped<S, T>` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per step; \(O(1)\).; traps: when `k < 1`
- `@get fn even<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T>(self: S) -> Stepped<S, T>` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per step; \(O(1)\).
- `@get fn odd<S: Indexed<K, T>, K, T>(self: S) -> Stepped<S, T>` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per step; \(O(1)\).
- `fn rekey<D, K, T>(self: [D]T, keys: Range<K>) -> [K]T` — \(O(n)\), allocates; \(O(n)\).; traps: when `keys.len != self.len`
- `fn collect<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\), allocates; The end of a lazy chain, materialized into the type the context expects, else a `List`.
- `fn keyed<S: Seq<T>, I: Indexed, T, K>(self: S, keys: I = 0.., by: ?(T -> K) = None) -> Keys<S, I, T, K>` — \(O(1)\) to make, \(O(1)\) per step; `self` with keys attached, so it is `Keyed`: walking it still gives values, `.items` gives `(key, x)`, and `argmax`/`find` answer with keys.; traps: when both `keys` and `by` are given; when `keys` runs out first
- `fn take_while<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, keep: T -> Bool) -> yields T` — \(O(1)\) per step
- `fn drop_while<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, drop: T -> Bool) -> yields T` — \(O(1)\) per step
- `fn filter_map<S: Seq<T>, T, U>(self: S, f: T -> ?U) -> yields U` — \(O(1)\) per step
- `fn flat_map<S: Seq<T>, T, U: Seq<V>, V>(self: S, f: T -> U) -> yields V` — \(O(1)\) per yielded element
- `fn flatten<S: Seq<U>, U: Seq<T>, T>(self: S) -> yields T` — \(O(1)\) per yielded element
- `fn present<S: Seq<?U>, U>(self: S) -> yields U` — \(O(1)\) per step
- `fn all_some<S: Seq<?U>, U>(self: S) -> ?List<U>` — \(O(n)\), \(O(n)\) memory
- `fn chain<Ss, T>(..seqs: Ss) -> yields T` — \(O(1)\) per step
- `fn product<A: Seq<T>, B: Indexed<L, U>, L, T, U>(a: A, b: B) -> yields (T, U)` — \(O(1)\) per step, \(O(\lvert a \rvert \cdot \lvert b \rvert)\) to walk; \(O(1)\) per step.
- `fn iterate<T>(from: ?T, step: T -> ?T) -> yields T` — \(O(1)\) per step plus one call of `step`; \(O(1)\) per step.
- `fn with_next<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S) -> yields (T, ?T)` — \(O(1)\) per step
- `fn zip_exact<A: Indexed<K, T>, B: Positional<U>, K, T, U>(a: A, b: B) -> yields (T, U)` — \(O(1)\) per step; traps: when `a.len != b.len`
- `fn chunks_padded<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(self: S, k: 1.., pad: T) -> yields List<T>` — \(O(k)\) per chunk; \(O(n)\).; traps: when `k < 1`
- `fn contains<S: Seq<T>, T: Eq>(self: S, x: T) -> Bool` — \(O(n)\) comparisons; \(O(n)\).
- `fn reduce<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, f: (T, T) -> T) -> ?T` — \(O(n)\) calls of `f`; \(O(n)\).
- `fn fold<S: Seq<T>, T, M: FromOp<T>>(self: S, op: M) -> T` — \(O(n)\) calls of `op`; \(O(n)\).; traps: never (an `op` without a known identity is a compile-time error)
- `fn fold_from<S: Seq<T>, T, Acc>(self: S, init: Acc, f: (Acc, T) -> Acc) -> Acc` — \(O(n)\) calls of `f`; \(O(n)\).
- `fn max_count<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x) -> ?(val: T, count: Int)` — \(O(n)\)
- `fn min_count<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x) -> ?(val: T, count: Int)` — \(O(n)\)
- `fn majority<S: Seq<T>, T>(self: S, eq: (T, T) -> Bool = (a, b) => a == b) -> ?(val: T, count: Int)` — at most \(\lfloor 3n/2 \rfloor\) calls of `eq`; \(O(n)\) memory; The value held by more than half the elements, with its count, or `None`.
- `fn group<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord, U>(self: S, by: T -> K, of: T -> U = x => x) -> Map<K, List<U>>` — \(O(n \log n)\), \(O(n)\) memory
- `fn min_k<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: S, k: Len, by: T -> K = x => x) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\) expected, \(O(k)\) memory: one pass into a buffer of at most `2k`, cut back to `k` by `select` whenever it fills; \(O(n)\) expected, \(O(k)\) memory.; traps: when `k < 0` or `k >= 2^31`; `k > n` gives every element
- `fn max_k<S: Seq<T>, T, K: Ord>(self: S, k: Len, by: T -> K = x => x) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\) expected, \(O(k)\) memory: one pass into a buffer of at most `2k`, cut back to `k` by `select` whenever it fills; \(O(n)\) expected, \(O(k)\) memory.; traps: when `k < 0` or `k >= 2^31`; `k > n` gives every element
- `fn partition_in_place<S: IndexedMut<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(mut self: S, keep: T -> Bool) -> Int` — \(O(n)\), \(O(1)\) extra space; \(O(n)\).
- `fn stable_partition_in_place<S: IndexedMut<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(mut self: S, keep: T -> Bool) -> Int` — \(O(n)\), \(O(n)\) memory
- `fn adjacent_diff<S: Seq<T>, T: Sub>(self: S) -> List<T>` — \(O(n)\), \(O(n)\) memory
- `fn span<D>(lo: Cut<D>, hi: Cut<D>) -> Range<D>` — \(O(1)\); traps: when `lo > hi`
- `fn bsearch<D, T>(self: [D]T, ok: T -> Bool, last: Bool = false) -> Cut<D>` — \(O(\log n)\) calls of `ok`, plus one when the cut is an end; \(O(\log n)\).; traps: when `ok` flips the other way; any other `ok` that is not monotone gives an
- `fn equal_range<D, T, K: Ord>(self: [D]T, target: K, by: T -> K = x => x) -> Range<D>` — \(O(\log n)\); traps: a checked build may trap R0401 on unsorted input, whose search is then wrong-way;
- `fn count_in<D, T, K>(self: [D]T, r: Range<K>, by: T -> K = x => x) -> Int` — \(O(\log n)\); traps: a checked build may trap R0401 on unsorted input, whose search is then wrong-way;
- `fn sorted_union<A: Indexed, B: Indexed, T: Eq>(self: A, b: B) -> List<T>` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\), \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\) memory
- `fn sorted_intersect<A: Indexed, B: Indexed, T>(self: A, b: B) -> List<T>` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\), \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\) memory; The values in both of two sorted sequences, merged in one pass.
- `fn sorted_diff<A: Indexed, B: Indexed, T>(self: A, b: B) -> List<T>` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\), \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert b \rvert)\) memory
- `fn kway_merge<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(lists: List<S>) -> List<T>` — \(O(N \log k)\), \(O(N)\) memory
- `fn radix_sort<S: IndexedMut<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(mut self: S, by: T -> Int = x => x)` — \(O(n)\) passes over 8-bit digits of the key, \(O(n)\) memory; \(O(n)\), \(O(n)\) memory.
- `fn counting_sort<S: IndexedMut<D, T>, D: Domain, T, K>(mut self: S, by: T -> K)` — \(O(n + \lvert K \rvert)\), \(O(n + \lvert K \rvert)\) memory; Sorts in place by `by(x)`, a position of the domain `K`, keeping equal keys in their order: one count per position of `K`, then each element goes to its slot.
- `fn is_permutation<A: Seq<T>, B: Seq<T>, T: Hash + Eq>(self: A, b: B) -> Bool` — \(O(n)\) expected, \(O(n)\) memory
- `fn is_subsequence<S: Seq<T>, N: Indexed, T>(self: S, of: N) -> Bool` — \(O(\lvert \mathit{self} \rvert + \lvert \mathit{of} \rvert)\)
- `fn perm_rank<V>(self: [V]V) -> Int` — \(O(n)\), \(O(1)\) memory; traps: when `|V| > 20` or `p` is not a permutation
- `fn perm_unrank<V>(rank: Int) -> [V]V` — \(O(n \log n)\), \(O(1)\) memory beyond the result; traps: when `rank` is not in `0..|V|!`
- `fn perm_sign<V>(self: [V]V) -> Int` — \(O(n)\), \(O(n)\) memory; traps: when `p` is not a permutation
- `fn perm_order<V>(self: [V]V) -> Int` — \(O(n)\), \(O(n)\) memory; traps: never; the order can overflow `Int` past about |V| = 400
- `fn partial_inverse<I, V>(self: [I]?V) -> [V]?I` — \(O(\lvert I \rvert + \lvert V \rvert)\), \(O(\lvert I \rvert + \lvert V \rvert)\) memory; traps: when two keys map to the same value
- `fn combinations<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(self: S, k: Len) -> yields List<T>` — \(O(k)\) per combination; traps: when `k < 0` or `k >= 2^31`
- `fn index_pairs<D>(self: Range<D>) -> yields (D, D)` — \(O(1)\) per pair
- `fn permutations<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(self: S, k: ?Int = None) -> yields List<T>` — \(O(k)\) per permutation; traps: when `k` is not in `0..=self.len`
- `fn subsequences<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T>(self: S) -> yields SubseqStep<T>` — \(O(k)\) per subsequence
- `fn lis<D, T, K: Ord>(self: [D]T, strict: Bool = true, by: T -> K = x => x) -> List<D>` — \(O(n \log n)\), \(O(n)\) memory
- `fn lcs<A: Indexed, B: Indexed, T>(a: A, b: B) -> List<(Int, Int)>` — \(O(\lvert a \rvert \cdot \lvert b \rvert)\), \(O(\lvert a \rvert \cdot \lvert b \rvert)\) memory
- `fn cartesian_tree<D, T: Ord>(self: [D]T, min_root: Bool = true) -> (root: ?D, left: [D]?D, right: [D]?D, parent: [D]?D)` — \(O(n)\), \(O(n)\) memory
- `fn argmax<S: Keyed<D, T>, D, T, K: Ord>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x, ties: Ties = Ties.First) -> ?D` — \(O(n)\); The index of the first largest value (optionally under key `by:`), or `None` when empty.
- `fn argmin<S: Keyed<D, T>, D, T, K: Ord>(self: S, by: T -> K = x => x, ties: Ties = Ties.First) -> ?D` — \(O(n)\); The index of the first smallest value (optionally under key `by:`), or `None` when empty.
- `@get fn swap<A>(self: (A, A)) -> (A, A)` — \(O(1)\)
- `fn split<S: Indexed<D, T>, D: Domain, T, P: Sep<T>>(self: S, sep: P) -> yields Slice<S>` — \(O(n)\); Pieces between separators: elements equal to `sep`, or where the predicate `sep` holds.
- `fn maximal<D, T, St: Track<T>>(self: [D]T, state: St, ok: St -> Bool, anchor: Anchor = Anchor.End) -> [D]Range<D>` — \(O(n)\) amortized pushes and pops on `state`; Two pointers: for each right end, the longest piece ending there that is `ok`, fed through `state: Track`, as its positions.; traps: never in release; debug traps when `ok` fails on a single element after a shrink
- `fn minimal<D, T, St: Track<T>>(self: [D]T, state: St, ok: St -> Bool, anchor: Anchor = Anchor.End) -> [D]?Range<D>` — \(O(n)\) amortized pushes and pops on `state`; For each right end, the shortest piece ending there that is `ok` (its positions), or None, keyed by that end like the ring forms; `anchor: Anchor.Start` keys by left end.
- `@get fn ring<D, T>(self: [D]T) -> Ring<D, T>` — \(O(1)\); \(O(1)\) to make.
- `fn valleys<D, T: Ord>(self: [D]T) -> yields Range<D>` — \(O(n)\) to walk; The non-empty ranges whose every element is strictly below both elements just outside it (both must exist).
- `fn spans<D, T, K>(self: [D]T, by: T -> K = x => x) -> [D]Range<D>` — \(O(n)\); For each position, the widest piece where it is the minimum of `by` (ties: the left one extends).
- `fn prev_smaller<D, T, K: Ord>(self: [D]T, by: T -> K = x => x, strict: Bool = true) -> [D]?D` — \(O(n)\); Nearest earlier position with a smaller key (`strict: false`: smaller or equal).
- `fn next_smaller<D, T, K: Ord>(self: [D]T, by: T -> K = x => x, strict: Bool = true) -> [D]?D` — \(O(n)\); Nearest later position with a smaller key.
- `fn prev_same<D, T, K: Hash + Eq>(self: [D]T, by: T -> K = x => x) -> [D]?D` — \(O(n)\) expected; Nearest earlier position with an equal key.
- `fn next_same<D, T, K: Hash + Eq>(self: [D]T, by: T -> K = x => x) -> [D]?D` — \(O(n)\) expected; Nearest later position with an equal key.
- `fn outermost<D, S: Seq<Range<D>>>(self: S) -> List<Range<D>>` — \(O(n \log n)\); The ranges no other range contains, sorted by left end (ties: the first kept).
- `@get fn keys<T>(self: List<T>) -> Range<Int>` — \(O(1)\)

## Example

```cp
let xs = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]
print(xs.sorted(), xs.sum(), inversions(xs))
// output: 1 1 3 4 5 14 3
```
